miguel_pm: FYI — after last week's capacity incident I drafted a focused PRD delta to clarify SLA scope, launch criteria, and required runbook updates. Need quick review + scope signoff before EOW.

anna_prod: skimmed it. TL;DR: tighten P95/P99, define automatic fallback behavior, add rollback triggers. short on time but can review ACs tonight. :thumbsup:

sam_engineering: the fallback rule as written will require changes in router + model catalog. estimate 3 dev-weeks if we do full-model fallback chain. Can we reduce scope to "single-step fallback" for initial rollout?

clarice_sre: strongly +1 on runbook additions. we should add explicit thresholds and alert text so oncall knows whether to scale, route, or kick to manual. propose new monitoring metrics: `inflight_tokens`, `queue_depth`, `fallback_rate`.

kevin_support: customer ask (Atlas): they expect documented behavior when dedicated pool is saturated, and they want a hard SLA for failover to hosted. If we push single-step fallback we can make an explicit contractual statement. Atlas flagged this as deal blocker.

miguel_pm: thanks. propose compromise: PRD change =
```
Acceptance Criteria (delta):
- P95 latency target defined per route (default 200ms). Customers can pin route-specific SLOs.
- When dedicated capacity per-customer > 85% for 60s, initiate single-step fallback to pinned lower-cost model variant.
- Fallback must preserve request order and return a `x-redwood-fallback: model-variant` header in responses.
- Automatic fallback must be recorded as a discrete event in audit logs and surfaced in console incidents view.
- Rollback criteria: if fallback_rate > 3% for 5m OR error_rate increases by > 0.5pp, auto-revert to original routing and open pager.
- Runbook additions: playbook section "fallback-on-saturation" with exact alert thresholds and one-command mitigation steps.
```

anna_prod: these ACs look actionable. request: include an edge-case note for streaming sessions — streaming should be disabled during fallback and clients must receive a 308-like notice header to re-connect.

sam_engineering: implementable but needs updates to streaming layer + sdk behavior. I'll add an engineering estimate to the PR (likely 2 sprints for streaming-safe fallback). For now we can scope to non-streaming routes for v1.

clarice_sre: add to runbook: immediate actions for oncall:
- check `fallback_rate` over 1m and 5m
- if P95 > target AND fallback_rate > 1% -> run `scripts/force-routing-fallback.sh customer-id` (one-liner in runbook)
- escalate to infra if `queue_depth` > 1000

kevin_support: I'll draft a short customer note that maps our single-step fallback promise to billing/SLAs. want to avoid overpromising full multi-tier failover.

miguel_pm: good. next steps:
- @sam_engineering: add scope & timeline to PR by EOD tomorrow. mark non-streaming-only if needed.
- @clarice_sre: submit runbook patch PR with command snippets and alert wording by Wed.
- @kevin_support: draft Atlas customer note and share with legal for wording.
- @anna_prod: final AC approval once engineering scope is attached.

deploy-bot: Reminder: PRD delta draft uploaded: https://redwood.internal/prds/1789-sla-fallback-delta (CI: 3 checks pending)

anna_prod: acked. I'll do a quick read after standup. :eyes:

miguel_pm: thanks team — aim to sync on Thursday 11:00 for final signoff. I'll also add a short section in the product roadmap doc to mark this as "post-incident hardening" and a priority-2 initiative.

sam_engineering: noted, will flag any blocking infra work ASAP so we can negotiate timeline with product.

clarice_sre: one more edge-case: customers with strict VPC/on-prem private deployments might not accept cross-traffic fallback. suggest an opt-out flag in customer config and a required consent doc for any fallback that routes off-prem.

miguel_pm: good catch — add opt-out AC: "private deployments may opt-out of automated fallback; opt-out must be explicit and recorded in account config; if opted out, increase manual escalation SLA to 5m."

kevin_support: documented. sending Atlas the draft note now. will move to legal after they ack the phrasing.

miguel_pm: closing loop — once PR + runbook + customer note land, we'll schedule a canary in lower-tier customers for 1 week and monitor metrics. If metrics look good, we roll to Dedicated customers with a 2-week notice window.

anna_prod: sounds good, thanks all.
